key_insight: AD-WM learns a world model that does not just predict what will happen, but also separates and ranks different actions from the same state. This makes counterfactual model predictive control more reliable when choosing among competing actions.
problem_solved: Standard latent world models are trained on factual transitions, so they can predict the next state well while still failing to distinguish which action is actually better. This is a problem for MPC, which needs accurate counterfactual comparisons between candidate actions starting from the same state.
method: Uses a joint-embedding world model with residual latent dynamics to improve transition modeling.
Adds predictor-level action-recovery regularization so the model preserves action-discriminative information.
Leverages inverse dynamics and a normalized representation objective to better separate counterfactual action outcomes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, AD-WM offers a more decision-aware world model for planning and control. It can improve action selection in MPC settings where small differences between candidate actions matter, especially in robotics and sequential decision-making.

paper_title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control
paper_authors: Jiabin Qiu, Zixuan Chen, Hongye Cao, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo
